newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp debt issuers proceed with caution.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp debt issuers proceed with caution.

text.p: Spurred by renewed fears of higher U.S. interest rates, issuers are expected to throw caution to the wind and finance their deals now, ahead of what some anticipate will be a tougher rate environment ahead, dealers said.
"The market will see a few more names come this week but these deals will have a lot more size to them," said one syndicate source.
Among upcoming offerings are J.C. Penney's $2.0 billion multi-tranche debt offering, which some dealers said may grow in size to 3.0 billion.
The Penney deal is expected to include five-, 10- and 30-year maturities. Credit Suisse First Boston is expected to serve as lead manager for the deal, sources said.
Another $1.0 billion in 10-year debt is expected to come from Asian Development Bank, sources said. Goldman Sachs & Co is expected to underwrite that deal.
"There's still a cautious tone in the marketplace," said one syndicate source. "We have to see how last week's deals were accepted, what their reception is this week and how they trade."
"We're still testing the waters...each deal will be a new adventure," the syndicate source added.
Meanwhile, Hilton Hotels has come on the scene with a $300 million 10-year note deal, which carries a coupon reset provision in the event of a downgrade, sources said.
The reset provision consists of the following breakdown, according to market sources.
Moody's /S&P Spread
Ba1 /BB-plus 175 basis points over Treasuries
Ba2 /BB 210 basis points over Treasuries
Ba3 /BB-minus 250 basis points over Treasuries
B1 /B-plus or below 325 basis points over Treasuries
The Baa1/BBB-plus rated Hilton offering is expected to be underwritten by Merrill Lynch & Co.

In the high-yield primary sector, a two-part offering from Triton Energy Corp, a unit of Triton Energy Ltd, including $200 million each of five- and 30-year debt was expected to come to market this week via Bear Stearns & Co and Salomon Brothers.
Price talk on the five year issue is seen between 162.5 and 175 basis points, and price talk on the 10-year is 195 to 200 basis points, sources said.
Also, Syratech Corp is expected to issue $155 million in 10-year senior notes via Nationsbanc Capital Markets, sources said.
Another $100 million in B2/B rated 10-year issue via Bway Corp. BT Securities is expected to underwrite the offering, sources said. Price talk on the deal is between 300-325 basis points, they added.
Other names include: Anchor Glass Container's $150 million, Consumer International's $170 million and Greyhound Lines Inc's $150 million, 144A private placement offerings.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury 30-year bond is trading up 17/32 at 94-13/32 to yield 7.08 percent compared with 7.12 percent at Friday's close.
